articles.title: Gordon Ryan issues statement on ‘fun’ ADCC 2026 brawl, two BJJ stars suspended
articles.summary: Dorian Olivarez has been disqualified for the ADCC 2026 brawl, which saw Gordon Ryan getting “jumped.”
articles.body:
While Day 1 of ADCC has produced a lot of beautiful submissions , it's the ugly brawl involving Gordon Ryan , Dorian Olivarez and Bezkat Kapashov that's getting the most attention.

After Olivarez got a submission win over Kapashov, a brawl erupted between him the large Kazakh contingent supporting Kapashov. Olivarez's coach and teammate Gordon Ryan seems to have gotten the worst of it, as the Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) all-time great took punches from multiple attackers in the melee.

Gordon Ryan releases statement on ADCC 2026 brawl

Minutes after getting backstage, Gordon Ryan immediately released a statement and described his side of the brawl .

"John (Danaher) and Mike (Olivarez, Dorian's father) are in their 50s, so it's just the three of them and like 15 Kazakh guys," Ryan said, explaining that he was cornering a different teammate on the next mat. "This was all happening and I was like 'for sure, when this match is over there will be a fight. 100%.' I angle my chair towards them, while I was still coaching. The match ends, and a fight starts.

"15 Kazakh dudes jumped John, Mike and Dorian. [Editor's note: Danaher was on the side, and didn't seem to be involved at any point.] So I jump in. I crack the first guy," Ryan said. "The second guy sees me and yells, 'Gordon, Gordon, Gordon' They all turn towards me… immediately tackle me. Five or like six guys started hitting me in the head. One guy started soccer kicking me, a couple of guys punching me."

Ryan also called it a "fun" scrap that stole the show.

"(After it got broken up) the fight's done, I just run back, sat down and started coaching Dominic (Mejia)," Ryan said.

"Thanks to the Kazakh guys for the scrap. That was fun. Always remember, I'm fight of the night, every night."

Dorian Olivarez disqualified, suspended after ADCC 2026 brawl; Owen Jones steps in

While Dorian Olivarez got a nice submission win in the match, ADCC officials have announced that he won't be continuing in the tournament. Both him and Kapashov have been disqualified and suspended for their involvement in the brawl.

"As per ADCC, Dorian Olivarez and Bekzat Kapashov have been disqualified from the ADCC World Championship for their conduct on and off the mat. Both athletes will receive a one year ban from ADCC," FloGrappling announced .

After the suspension, Owen Jones will now step into Dorian's spot in the -66 kg tournament. The former B-Team star lost a close and controversial decision to Ryoma Anraku in the opening round, and will now get a second chance at the tourney.

Olivarez was initially one of the favorites to win the tournament, and has now lost his chance at an ADCC medal.

articles.title: Red Sox reactions: Sonny Gray hit hard, bats go quiet as Boston loses third straight
articles.summary: The Royals came out swinging against Sonny Gray on Friday night and the Red Sox couldn't climb out of an early deficit as they lost their third straight game...
articles.body:
BOSTON — Instant reactions to the Red Sox (80-68) falling behind early to the last-place Royals and taking their third straight loss, this time by a 3-2 score:

1) Sonny Gray put together a very unlikely quality start that started with rocket after rocket off the bats of Royals hitters and ended with a very respectable line. Gray was tagged for three runs and five hits in his first three innings, then allowed just three baserunners (and one hit) the rest of the way to keep the Sox in the game.

Still, it was too little too late after Gray was hit exceedingly — and concerningly — hard early as a bad Royals team hit eight balls with an exit velocity of 102.4 mph or harder and jumped out to a 3-0 lead.

Carter Jensen led off the game with a 110 mph double to center, then scored with two outs when Salvador Perez roped a single (103.9 mph) down the third base line. In the third, Isaac Collins led off with a ground-rule double (103.2 mph) before Jensen went high off the Green Monster with another two-bagger (102.6 mph) to make it 2-0. Vinnie Pasquantino 's RBI single (102.4 mph) made it 3-0.

In total, Gray struck out five and walked two.

2) Quietly, the Red Sox are not playing very well at home again. They've lost five of their last seven at Fenway Park — against three teams well under .500. On the whole, they are back to below .500 at home (36-37) this season. A defeat either Saturday or Sunday will mark the Sox' third straight series loss at Fenway.

3) To get the Sox on the board in the fifth, Mickey Gasper broke an 0-for-14 slump in a fitting way. He took Seth Lugo deep into the home bullpen for his ninth homer in 21 games since August 17. Somehow, some way... Gasper is now sixth on the team in home runs this season.

After failing to get much going against Lugo early, Boston's hitters saw him much better in a two-run fifth. Adley Rutschman walked, then scored on a Wilyer Abreu double that hit high up on the Green Monster and made it a one-run game.

4) In a one-run game, the Sox did little against a cast of unknown characters in Kansas City 's bullpen. Nolan Hoffman (ninth MLB game) and lefty Connor Thomas (14th MLB game) needed just 24 total pitches for back-to-back perfect innings in the sixth and seventh. Righty Nate Pearson then dispatched the middle of the order in an eighth inning that didn't come without drama.

Trevor Story smoked a 105 mph one-out double off the Green Monster and took second on a close play, avoiding a tag attempt with a nifty slide. The Sox couldn't do anything with that chance, though, as Nick Sogard lifted a fly ball to deep right field (that would have been a homer in half of baseball's parks) and Caleb Durbin struck out chasing a pitch in the dirt.

In the ninth, hard-throwing righty Steven Cruz got three quick outs on a total of 10 pitches. He struck out Roman Anthony to end it.

5) Overall, it was a poor offensive night for the Sox. The lineup combined to go 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position and left eight on base. Boston had eight hits but just three extra-base hits (the Gasper homer and the doubles by Abreu and Story). Boston's batters struck out 10 times and walked just twice.

6) Jarren Duran is within one steal of the second 20-20 season of his career. He stole second base in the fourth inning for his 19th robbery of the season and already has 20 homers. Considering Duran hasn't felt like himself at the plate all season, it's a notable accomplishment that he has still been able to consistently tap into both power and speed all season.

7) Gray's chances of a first-career 20-win season dwindled significantly as he fell to 17-5 with the loss . With 14 regular season games to go and the Red Sox still overwhelmingly likely to make the postseason, he'll likely only start twice more as Boston tries to line up its rotation for the wild card round. Gray will likely make his next start in Tampa Bay next week and pitch once on the final homestand of the year. He remains the favorite to pitch Game 1 of the postseason.

Gray is tied for the MLB-lead in wins with Philadelphia lefty Cristopher Sánchez and leads the American League on his own. Next up in the AL is Tampa Bay's Nick Martinez (14).

8) The Sox and Royals will play again Saturday in the middle game of a three-game set between the clubs. First pitch is at 4:10 p.m. ET with lefty Ranger Suarez (6-4, 3.44 ERA) starting opposite Kansas City right-handers Randy Dobnak (3-3, 2.54 ERA).

articles.title: Dan Lanning, Pat McAfee team up for massive charity donation
articles.summary: Dan Lanning conquered Pat McAfee's challenge on 'College Gameday' to score a massive donation for charity.
articles.body:
Dan Lanning is laser-focused on helping the Oregon Ducks take down Oklahoma State on the road this Saturday, but that doesn't mean he can't help contribute toward a good cause off the field as well.

During a pregame interview on ' College Gameday,' Lanning walked the field at Boone Pickens Stadium while chatting with the hosts of the famous pregame show. Kirk Herbstreit noticed Lanning was holding a football near the goal line and pushed for fellow host Pat McAfee to issue a challenge to the Oregon coach.

"I'm juiced up, man," Lanning said. "I'm hoping we can raise a little money for something, Pat."

McAfee, always generous with his fortune, backed the challenge. If Lanning could throw the ball and hit the crossbar from the 10-yard line (a 20-yard throw), McAfee would donate $500,000 to the charity of Lanning's choice.

Lanning missed on the first throw, but McAfee gave him another chance, backing up to the 15-yard line. Oregon has improved every season under Lanning, and the coach improved on his next chance as well. Lanning bounced the ball off the crossbar and landed the big score.

McAfee's massive donation will go to the Sam Day Foundation, a charity focused on research surrounding childhood cancer. Lanning has worked with the foundation in the past, most recently raising money through Cameo and sending personalized videos to fans and donating the money to the charity. Lanning targeted $50,000 for the challenge, but wound up raising $100,000 instead.

Lanning didn't let McAfee donate alone. The Ducks ' leader added $50,000 of his own to the pot for a cause that is near and dear to him and his family.

In 2024, Oregon wore yellow uniforms designed by the Lanning family to honor his wife, Sauphia, who has been cancer-free since 2017. A portion of the retail proceeds from the " Heroes" uniform collection went straight to the University of Oregon's Knight Campus for Accelerating Scientific Impact and the Oregon Cancer Foundation.

Lanning has scored big off the field, and now will look to score big on it. The Ducks are set for an early kickoff in Stillwater against Oklahoma State in the first road test of the season.

articles.title: US Open Final Preview: Ben Shelton Faces Alexander Zverev for New York Glory
articles.summary: And then there were two, as after almost a fortnight of high-octane tennis at the US Open, we have a final set, as the No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev is set to...
articles.body:
And then there were two, as after almost a fortnight of high-octane tennis at the US Open , we have a final set, as the No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev is set to face off against the No. 1 American men's player, Ben Shelton.

The two players have separated themselves from the others over the course of the tournament, and now they eye one of the biggest prizes in tennis. Zverev is looking to add another Slam to his resume quickly after winning his first , while Shelton is trying to become the first American men's player since Andy Roddick over two decades ago to win a Major title.

And we here at LWOT will be bringing you an in-depth preview of what to expect in one of the biggest matches of the year.

While both players have had to work hard to make the final, their paths to it have been as different as possible. Handed a brutal draw that saw him face three former top-10 players in his first four matches, Shelton did brilliantly to manage the initial tough tests. He then had the win of his life in the quarterfinals, when he defeated Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic to make the semifinals, where he took out fellow countryman Frances Tiafoe in a much more comfortable match than many had expected.

His opponent in the final, Zverev, has had one of the historically softer draws leading up to a Slam final ever, as he is yet to play anyone ranked inside the top-20 in the world. The German did make his life tougher in the early matches, playing back-to-back five-setters to start the tournament, but since then he has been spotless, winning all of his matches in straight sets to make the final, where he will get a matchup that he has historically dominated, winning all five of his matches played against Shelton so far .

Why Zverev Has Historically Dominated This Matchup

The main reason this matchup is one-sided is that Zverev has the perfect game to expose Shelton's weaknesses: his big serve often causes problems for Shelton, a below-average returner, while Zverev's elite backhand can make Shelton's baseline inconsistencies show up. Zverev has historically had great success against left-handed players because he is one of the few players who feels more confident off his backhand side than his forehand.

This means that in the traditional cross-court exchange, the lefty player's forehand ends up being in a battle with Zverev's backhand, with the German more often than not being not only more consistent in that pattern, but also more penetrating, as his backhand eventually takes its toll on the opponent during rallies. This results in either the lefty player making unforced errors or dropping a ball short that Zverev can easily put away, and this has been quite prevalent during the German's matches against Shelton.

However, this tournament so far, Shelton has shown great progress in both of these areas. The American is not only winning more of the break points he has generated this tournament compared to his past 52-week averages, but he is also winning more points on return, showing growth in an area that was needed for the American to truly take a step forward in his game.

Can Shelton's Improvements Change the Pattern?

Along with that, Shelton has been both mentally and physically outstanding this tournament so far, showing maturity in longer rallies that wasn't seen consistently before this tournament. The American has taken a more percentage-based approach, as instead of looking for the winners, he has been content with keeping the ball in when needed and going for the point-winning shot at the right time. This saw him win a higher volume of longer rallies against Alcaraz and Tiafoe than what was expected.

This does not mean the American is now pushing the ball in, but more that he is trusting his defensive skills and using his aggression in a more focused manner, either up at the net or when there is a clear opening from the back of the court.

Both of these adjustments should help him against Zverev, especially when you add in the factor that the bigger the match, the more tense the German is. Despite this being Zverev's sixth Slam final, it is still expected that he will be quite nervous not only to begin the match but also in the pressure moments. If that is the case, and Shelton can manage his own nerves while playing the biggest match of his career in front of a packed home crowd, things can definitely get more interesting than what the one-sided head-to-head might suggest.

History will be on the line for either player on Sunday, in what is definitely a final that many people had not expected to get going into the tournament. For Zverev, a win would mean all the ghosts of past heartbreaking defeats at the biggest stages are now firmly gone, as he not only gets his second Major title but can make a real push for the No. 1 ranking.

For Shelton, a win would welcome him into the tennis elite. Although he will not quite be at a stage where you could add him as the third one along with Alcaraz and Sinner, it would separate him from the rest of the players in his age group, giving him pole position to eventually be the consensus third-best player of the post-2000-born players era so far. It would also be the first-ever Major title won by an American men's player in more than two decades, as one of the longest waits for American tennis comes to an end, by a player who, despite his inconsistencies at times, has shown that he has the higher floor with his explosive game.

In the final Slam match of the year, all eyes will be on whether Shelton can rise to the occasion, or if the more experienced player comes out on top. Who do you think will prevail in New York on Sunday?

articles.title: Nets' Ben Saraf lays out his goals for second season in the NBA
articles.summary: Brooklyn Nets guard Ben Saraf is hoping to have a better time on the court during his second NBA season and he laid out his goals along the way.
articles.body:
Brooklyn Nets guard Ben Saraf is coming off a rookie season where he showed some glimpses of why he was a first-round pick while also displaying why he was taken outside of the Lottery. Brooklyn took Saraf as part of a five-man 2025 NBA Draft class and while he still has to earn his minutes, he still has other goals for what he wants to achieve this upcoming season.

"I think this year we want to win as many games as possible. Last season, there were more opportunities for the younger players, and I think that really helped all of us," Saraf said, per Joshua Halickman of The Jerusalem Post. Saraf was one of the young players that saw plenty of playing time last season, but he's also thinking about his team at the same time.

"But this year it's about winning. Whoever helps the team win is going to play. So for me, it's about earning minutes, earning the coaching staff's trust and being as impactful as I can," Saraf continued before providing an even more lofty goal for Brooklyn. "Making the playoffs is definitely a dream. I think this year our team has been built well, and I really believe we can do it. That's our goal."

Saraf, 20 , averaged 7.5 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game while shooting 39.6% from the field and 21.1% from behind the three-point line in 44 games played for the Nets last season. Saraf showed some improvement in Brooklyn's summer circuit this year as he averaged 10.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 37.3% from the floor and 33.3% from deep.

With the Nets selecting guard Mikel Brown Jr. with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Saraf will be competing with Brown and Nolan Traore for minutes at the point guard spot. Saraf will begin his quest for more minutes when training camp begins later this month and it seems that he's trying to achieve multiple goals this season, both personal and team-wise.

articles.title: Dave Roberts Explains Dodgers’ Decision to End Eric Lauer’s Season
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers lefty Eric Lauer is out for the season, and manager Dave Roberts broke down the decision for the team.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers lefty Eric Lauer is out for the season, and manager Dave Roberts broke down the decision for the team.

To make room for Josue De Paula on the 40-man roster, the Dodgers put Lauer on the 60-day injured list , ruling him out for the rest of the season.

Lauer has been battling elbow inflammation, which put him on the 15-day IL starting September 2nd.

The lefty has been doing a throwing program, but the team didn't feel confident he could build up to be a starter.

With their bullpen full, Lauer would not have a role unless he was a piggyback-type option, but that was not happening with his elbow issue.

"We just felt we couldn't build him up enough to be a starter. He's just in the middle of his throwing program, and then I think for us, he's close, but I think in his role we're pretty set in the bullpen and so what we would need is something with the starter, in that kind of realm," Roberts said of Lauer.

"With the time that we have on the calendar, we just didn't have enough time, but he's trending in the right way though."

Lauer joined the Dodgers after the Toronto Blue Jays designated him for assignment, putting him on waivers, and LA agreed to a minor trade with Toronto to avoid the claim process.

The Dodgers were seriously lacking starting pitching, with Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell both out of action, and the need for a six-man rotation.

Lauer took the ball as the back-end starter, and he delivered high-quality production in that role.

He finished with a 4.50 ERA, a 7-2 record, and a total of 72 innings.

While pitching wins aren't a wholly representative statistic, for such a low-cost addition, the fact that the Dodgers won so many games with Lauer on the mound speaks to his ability to keep the team competitive in most of them.

Here's how Chicagoland high school football teams fared in Week 4 of play.

Junior tight end Ty Kennedy is emerging as yet another playmaker for the Caravan. He hauled in four catches for 66 yards and two touchdowns Friday night as host Mount Carmel pulled away late for a 56-26 Catholic League Blue win over Marist in Chicago.

Brady Cloherty completed 18 of 33 passes for 295 yards and five TDs for the Caravan (4-0, 1-0), which scored 28 points over the final eight minutes after the RedHawks pulled within 28-20.

Homewood-Flossmoor's Vito Pickard definitely made his point for host H-F, coming through with five tackles and scoring a touchdown on a fumble return in a 35-13 SouthWest Suburban Conference win over the Eagles.

Senior quarterback Rahsaan Coleman connected on a 64-yard TD pass to junior receiver John Gadson to spark the Vikings (3-1, 1-1), who bounced back from a 38-7 loss to Lincoln-Way East.

Lockport's Griffin Russell threw for 221 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another TD in a 38-15 SouthWest Suburban Conference victory over previously undefeated Lincoln-Way West.

Russell threw TD passes to Andrew Maloney for 30 yards, Donavan Gray for 32 yards and Jaxson Little for 10 yards to lead the Porters (1-3, 1-1), Russell set up the TD to Little with a 41-yard connection, also to Little. Prince Nartey added a 54-yard TD run.

Junior running back Aiden Brunner scored a pair of touchdowns in the second half — including the game-winner with 1.8 seconds left — as Jacobs erased a 17-point deficit in earning a 31-27 Fox Valley Conference win at Burlington Central.

Brunner finished with 38 yards on 11 carries for Jacobs (4-0, 4-0), including TDs of 1 and 8 yards. Austin Stennett led the comeback by completing 19 of 31 passes for 263 yards with a 74-yard TD to Owen Crouch, who ended with five catches for 111 yards. Chris Williams added seven catches for 59 yards and scored an 8-yard TD on a reverse. Jordan Hudson had five catches for 75 yards.

Naperville North 21, Naperville Central 14

The 5-foot-9, 170-pound Jayke Collins had his greatest game yet Friday night. He rushed 25 times for 136 yards and three touchdowns, all career highs, to lift the Huskies to a 21-14 victory over rival Naperville Central in a DuPage Valley Conference opener at North Central College.

According to Naperville North athletic director Jon Pereiro, a capacity crowd of 6,000 showed up at Benedetti-Wehrli Stadium. They were treated to a gritty performance by Collins, who dazzled in his first crosstown game as the Huskies (3-1, 1-0) earned their third straight win.

Zion-Benton's Kevin James knows defenses are going to try to stop teammate Jamere French, an Ohio recruit who is one of the best running backs in the area.

James suspects opponents don't believe the Zee-Bees can win another way.

Zion-Benton did exactly that during a North Suburban Conference game against visiting Stevenson on Thursday night. While French ran for 297 yards and four touchdowns on 38 carries, James caught two touchdown passes from quarterback Marquan Gordon in the unbeaten Zee-Bees' 42-23 win.

A game that featured very few punts was crying out for someone to make a defensive impact, and Prospect senior safety Caden Moran filled that void.

Moran made three interceptions on Thursday — two in the end zone that thwarted Fremd drives and then one that set up the touchdown that put the Knights up by two scores.

Indeed, Moran and Prospect made a statement by beating Fremd 35-21 in a Mid-Suburban League crossover between two undefeated teams.

Montini quarterback Israel Abrams passed for 412 yards and four TDs, including the go-ahead 33-yard pass to Damacio Ortegon with 34 seconds left, and also ran for three TDs.

It was big play after big play, and the Broncos (3-1), who are No. 11 in the Chicago Tribune's rankings, needed every one of them to hold off No. 21 Nazareth (1-3) as quarterback JJ Chapman threw for 301 passing yards and three scores.

articles.title: Eagles news: Why Nick Sirianni is sending OC to booth in Week 1 vs. Commanders
articles.summary: For the first time in five years, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is sending offensive coordinator Sean Mannion to the booth ahead of their Week...
articles.body:
For the first time in five years, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is sending offensive coordinator Sean Mannion to the booth ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Washington Commanders . The Eagles announced their final Week 1 injury report before Sunday's game, where Philadelphia's coaching staff will add a new wrinkle from its typical approach.

Sirianni explained the reasoning behind sending Mannion to the booth as oppose to typically standing besides him on the sideline, per NBC's Pro Football Talk.

"We want to think through every situation to make sure that we're giving ourselves the best opportunity for us to win the game and be at our best," Sirianni said. "Also understanding that there is no right way to do it or wrong way to do it. There's many different ways to do it. I think we can get caught up so much, it's like, 'This is the only way to do it.'

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"You have conviction in what you believe, but there's many different things that can work and have worked. It's just about making the best decision, what's best for your football team and for you to do your job the best. That's how we went about it."

Nick Sirianni justifies Week 1 play-calling decision

Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion reflected on moving to the booth after the preseason where head coach Nick Sirianni first experimented with having his offensive coordinator calling plays from the booth. Mannion reflected on the decision after the Eagles' last preseason game, per 94WIP's Eliot Shorr-Parks.

"Ultimately, I just felt like after doing both, it was the best decision for our staff for communication with our quarterbacks, and the best decision for our team," Sirianni said. "It was a very valuable experience and I think we're in a good place moving into the season."

The Eagles lost 30-13 to the Bengals in their preseason finale.

articles.title: Dortmund extend perfect start with victory over neighbours Paderborn
articles.summary: There was a new look to Borussia Dortmund’s lineup as Fábio Silva and Serhou Guirassy started together upfront. Meanwhile, Ethan Nwaneri was handed his first...
articles.body:
There was a new look to Borussia Dortmund 's lineup as Fábio Silva and Serhou Guirassy started together upfront. Meanwhile, Ethan Nwaneri was handed his first start in Dortmund colors and the captain Nico Schlotterbeck returns from long-standing injury.

Silva and Guirassay were unplayable after the former subbed on in midweek against Villarreal , and it was the same combination that put them in front inside five minutes against newly-promoted Paderborn.

Guirassay was the provider this time as he sent the Portuguese youngster one-on-one with Nahuel Noll . Silva continued his record of a direct goal contribution in every game he has played this season with a tidy finish.

The two attackers combined once again at the half-hour mark, but Guirassy's goal was chalked off by VAR because of an offside call. The Guinean striker was also punished twice in promising situations inside the box.

Apart from Laurin Curda's chance in the 20th minute, the visitors were far from coming close to scoring their first goal of the season back in Bundesliga. And there was still time for one more Guirassy moment as the all-action striker was denied by VAR for the second time after scoring with a close-range header.

Guirassy continued to fashion the best chances after the restart, but Noll was solid in Paderborn's goal. At the end, it was substitute Felix Nmecha who succeeded in beating the shot-stopper with the assist also coming from substitute Maximilian Beier .

Nmecha completed his brace a minute before the end of regular time with a dream bicycle-kick strike. Paderborn are yet to score a goal after their first three games back in Bundesliga. Kovac's troops started the campaign with three victories.

Dortmund will travel to VfB Stuttgart in next week's Topspiel, while Paderborn will host Hoffenheim in the last Bundesliga game before the season's first international break.

As the Pittsburgh Steelers prepare for the 2026 regular season opener, their Week 1 opponent, the Atlanta Falcons , have ruled out four players for Sunday's game.

Thanks to Friday's injury report, we now know that the Falcons have ruled four players out for the Week 1 game against Pittsburgh: quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (oblique), quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (knee), cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. (Achilles), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle). Edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (shoulder) was deemed questionable.

Predicting Steelers' wins and losses for 2026 season

Tagovailoa, who joined the Falcons this offseason after spending six years with the Miami Dolphins , picked up a surprising oblique injury out of nowhere. He was primed for the starting opportunity but will now be forced to watch the matchup from the sidelines.

Penix being ruled out was expected, as he suffered a torn ACL last season and wasn't cleared for 11-on-11 practice until late August. He did manage to log full participation during three consecutive practices this week, but Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski revealed Penix would still be inactive in Week 1.

Bowman was promising for Atlanta as a rookie last year but unfortunately suffered a torn Achilles just six games into the season. He was a limited participant in practice this week but won't make his return against Pittsburgh.

Williams, a depth piece at offensive tackle for the Falcons, was claimed off waivers after he was released by the Philadelphia Eagles as part of final roster cuts. He is currently listed as the third-string offensive tackle, so his absence won't be a huge loss for Atlanta.

articles.title: Osborne makes history as first female jockey to win a Classic with St Leger victory
articles.summary: Saffie Osborne becomes the first female jockey to win a British Classic Flat race, claiming victory in the St Leger on Highwayman.
articles.body:
Saffie Osborne has become the first female jockey to win one of British Flat racing's five Classics, riding Highwayman to victory in the St Leger at Doncaster.

The 24-year-old burst clear of the field on the 11-1 chance in the closing stages to create history in the 250th anniversary of the world's oldest Classic Flat race.

It was a one-two for winning trainer Joseph O'Brien, whose colt Enceladus (5-2) finished second, two-and-a-half lengths back.

Aidan O'Brien was bidding to become just the third trainer to win a fourth consecutive St Leger but had to be content with third with Amelia Earhart (22-1).

Pre-race favourite Christmas Day (7-4) was heavily backed to give Aidan O'Brien that historic fourth victory in a row and complete the Derby-St Leger double, but finished well down in ninth place.

"I definitely didn't have this on the bingo card this week," Osborne told ITV Sport immediately after the historic victory in the fifth and final Classic of the British Flat season.

"I didn't even know if I would be riding the St Leger on Monday morning."

No female jockey has won any of the other four Classics - the 1,000 Guineas and 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket and the Oaks and Derby at Epsom.

Osborne was quick to thank the trainer for giving her the ride, adding: "I have to thank Joseph and his team for putting their faith in me. It won't change Joseph's life, but it's changed mine."

Joseph O'Brien won the St Leger as a jockey on Leading Light in 2013 and claimed his first victory as a trainer in 2020 with Galileo Chrome.

Enceladus was expected to be his best chance to double his number of winners in the famous old race, having hit top form this season with three big victories, including in the Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

But Highwayman had also showed rapid improvement this year, especially in winning the Vinnie Roe Stakes at Leopardstown.

articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka: Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2026 final – schedule, teams, form
articles.summary: Aiming for a record-extending eighth title, India take on defending champions Sri Lanka in Sunday’s final in Dubai.
articles.body:
Who : India vs Sri Lanka What : Women’s T20 Asia Cup final Where : Dubai International Stadium, Dubai, United Arab Emirates When : Sunday, September 13, 6:30pm local time (14:30 GMT) How to follow : We’ll have all the build-up on Al Jazeera Sport from 3:30pm local time (13:30 GMT) before our live text commentary stream.

Record seven-time winners India face defending champions Sri Lanka in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final on Sunday, as the 15-match competition in the United Arab Emirates readies itself for its closing act.

In a tournament which has largely yielded low-scoring contests, both Indian and Sri Lankan spin units have tasted success – Deepti Sharma spearheading the heavyweights’ charge and captain Chamari Athapaththu leading by example for the title holders.

Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana’s terrific top-order pairing has further strengthened India’s title bid at the tournament, where both teams boast a perfect record.

Having reached the final in every edition of the Women’s Asia Cup they have played, India are favourites to add another trophy to their glittering cabinet.

But Sri Lanka possess a threat of their own – they are one of only two sides who have beaten India in the title clash in past and will be eager to retain the trophy they proudly lifted two years ago.

Before Sunday’s showdown, Al Jazeera Sport takes a closer look at the game:

Who did India and Sri Lanka beat in the semifinals?

India defeated Bangladesh in the first semifinal on Thursday by 40 runs before Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by four wickets in Friday’s low-scoring thriller.

The pair last met in a T20 international in Thiruvananthapuram on December 30, 2025, as hosts India defeated Sri Lanka by 15 runs, sweeping that series 5-0.

Records swing heavily in India’s favour – they have won nine of their last 10 T20Is against Sri Lanka.

How many Women’s Asia Cup titles have India won?

India are the most successful team in the Women’s Asia Cup, having won a record seven titles.

They won the 2004, 2005, 2006 and 2008 editions, when the tournament was played in a one-day international format, as well as the 2012, 2016 and 2022 T20 editions.

How many Women’s Asia Cup titles have Sri Lanka won?

Sri Lanka have won the Women’s Asia Cup once, winning the last edition in 2024 after beating India by eight wickets in the final.

India’s openers Shafali and Mandhana are the top two leading scorers in the ongoing edition, having scored 168 and 154 runs each in four matches.

Shafali has registered two half-centuries – scoring identical 64s against Thailand in the opener and Bangladesh in the semifinals – while Mandhana hit an incredible 124 against Hong Kong in the league phase.

With the ball, all-rounder Deepti has been most impactful with her spin bowling, bagging a joint-highest 11 wickets with an average of 3.63.

N Shree Charani has also played a key role with eight wickets and holds the record for the second-most economical bowler (3.27).

Captain Athapaththu, who bowls right arm off-break, has been Sri Lanka’s most impactful player, sharing the honours of the most wickets with Deepti at 11, with an average of 5.36. Left-arm orthodox bowler Sugandika Kumari has also contributed with six wickets.

With the bat, top-order left-hander Harsthitha Samarawickrama has chipped in 89 runs for the fourth-highest scorer in the competition.

India’s Deepti Sharma : “[This] team doesn’t take any team lightly … We always think as a team, ‘How we can do better in each and every game. As a collective team performance, how we can do better.’”

Sri Lanka’s Chamari Athapaththu : “If we can execute our plans in the final, I think we can beat any team.”

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez tips “composed” teammate to be the future of Manchester United
articles.summary: 2 Leny Yoro was finally handed a start at centre-back on Thursday in Manchester United’s 4-0 win over Sabah Baku, with Michael Carrick finally bowing to pres...
articles.body:
Leny Yoro was finally handed a start at centre-back on Thursday in Manchester United 's 4-0 win over Sabah Baku, with Michael Carrick finally bowing to pressure.

Before that game, throughout pre-season and the opening few fixtures, Yoro had instead been used to fill in at right-back. While he did not quite struggle there, he was not a hit either; in fact, some worried he was approaching the role with a centre-back's instincts and looked uncomfortable.

There were calls , then, for Carrick to try him in his natural position, and against Sabah, he finally did. How right that decision proved to be.

Yoro duly delivered a quality performance. He looked composed from the first minute, comfortable receiving the ball under pressure, confident carrying it forward, and intelligent with his positioning.

He did more than defend; he actively helped the team control the game from the back. His physical side, too, now looks far less fragile, with his movement at the back and his ability to cover the full-back both proving commendable.

There were plenty of positives to take from that Yoro performance, which is why many will resonate with what Lisandro Martinez said afterwards.

Lisandro Martinez backs Leny Yoro to be the "future" of Man United

"Amazing performance from Leny," Martinez said as per Steven Railston .

"He played so well defensively, with the ball, being calm, being composed in every situation, one-vs-one.

"He's the future of this club, honestly. And we have to help him, you know."

Yoro needs to be in the conversation for Man United's central defence

While Yoro is unlikely to start the derby on Sunday, he has certainly given Carrick food for thought over his central-defensive options.

With more opportunities there, and better performances building on the Sabah showing, the Frenchman can gradually establish himself as a key man in United's central defence.

articles.title: Andy Roddick hopes the US Women’s final gets the ‘respect it deserves’ despite absence of Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula
articles.summary: The US Women’s Final between Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina is set to be an encounter between two of the best in the game. They will face each other at F...
articles.body:
The US Women's Final between Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina is set to be an encounter between two of the best in the game. They will face each other at Flushing Meadows in front of a crowd that would have been hoping the final would be an All American affair.

Aryna Sabalenka made her way to the final after beating Jessica Pegula in straight sets (7-5, 6-2). Meanwhile, Rybakina overcame former US Open champion Coco Gauff in three sets (3-6,6-4,6-4).

The World Number 1 and 2 denied Arthur Ashe a chance to see the 11th All American women's US Open final, and the first since 2017.

However, Andy Roddick has asked for everyone to respect the final between the two stars, although it does not feature the two American sensations.

Roddick is a former US Open winner and knows what it's like to play in front of a home crowd.

He won his only Grand Slam at Arthur Ashe in front of over 20,000 fans who were cheering for him in the final over Juan Carlos Ferrero.

Roddick is now actively involved in the sport, working in the media, and also has his podcast where he spoke about how the crowds needed to respect Sabalenka and Rybakina.

"I hope the crowd gives it the respect that it deserves, even though it's not Coco or Jess in the final," he said on his Served podcast.

"These are two phenomenal players. The number one for this week, and then it flips next week. So let's enjoy these champions.

"As Sabalenka goes for her fifth major, Rybakina goes for her third, the second this year. Implications for number one in the world, on the line for the year-end ranking. So, I can't wait to watch this match."

Sabalenka leads the head-to-head with 10 wins in 17 games; however, Rybakina was the winner when the two met at the Australian Open in January.

The current World Number 1 has not lost a game at the US Open for almost three years and is coming into the final with hopes of three-peating. The last player to achieve this feat was Serena Williams.

There were many questions around her form coming into the tournament, but she has put all of that to bed with her electric display throughout the US Open.

Sabalenka will be hoping to win the prestigious US Open trophy once again and bag her fifth Grand Slam 5th title, while Rybakina will be hoping to end her streak of dominance in the US and beat her to secure her third ever title.

articles.standfirst: La joven dupla disputará el título en Roland Garros frente a Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero tras firmar un triunfo sin fisuras en las semifinales
articles.summary: La joven dupla disputará el título en Roland Garros frente a Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero tras firmar un triunfo sin fisuras en las semifinales
articles.body: La unión entre Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo apostaba por la juventud y el talento de dos de las principales promesas del pádel profesional, y su rendimiento en pista ha confirmado el éxito del proyecto. En el Paris Major, su cuarto torneo como dupla, la madrileña y la navarra han alcanzado su tercera final tras superar con solidez a las número uno del ranking mundial. Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea afrontaban las semifinales con la oportunidad de ampliar su ventaja en la clasificación tras la eliminación en cuartos de final de Bea González y Paula Josemaría. Sin embargo, Fernández y Calvo impusieron su ritmo desde los compases iniciales en la pista Philippe-Chatrier. La solidez de Fernández en el volumen de juego y la efectividad de Calvo en el remate decantaron el primer set por 6-4. En el segundo parcial, la pareja dirigida desde el banquillo mantuvo la agresividad en sus tiros para distanciarse con un 5-1 favorable. Pese al intento de reacción de Triay y Brea, Fernández y Calvo abrocharon el set por 6-2 con su servicio, certificando el pase a la última ronda del segundo Major de la temporada. En el otro lado del cuadro, Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero lograron el segundo billete a la final tras remontar un exigente duelo ante Marta Ortega y Sofía Araújo, quienes venían de eliminar a las cabeza de serie número dos. Ortega y Araújo se adjudicaron la primera manga por 7-5 gracias a la firmeza defensiva de la jugadora madrileña y la potencia en el remate de la portuguesa. No obstante, Sánchez y Ustero incrementaron la intensidad en los siguientes parciales. El ajuste táctico y la eficacia en el juego aéreo de la reusense y la barcelonesa permitieron igualar el encuentro con un 6-4 en el segundo set. En la tercera y definitiva manga, la dupla catalana impuso un ritmo más alto para cerrar la victoria por 6-1, citándose este domingo con Fernández y Calvo en la lucha por el título.
